candidates.title: Aporium — map public-domain philosophy excerpts

ease.reason: The maker describes an interactive excerpt map, but a small version still needs data preparation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: educators or readers might pay; the source shows no demand or revenue.

feasibility.reason: A smaller map is possible, while embeddings and content curation add scope.

autonomy.reason: A generated map can be explored repeatedly; source selection and corrections need people.

evidence.reason: The maker describes a built 3D explorer and its excerpt pipeline, not independent use results.

candidates.reason: Requires substantial curation and technical work; the snapshot does not show a clear buyer or small business loop.

candidates.title: Modelship — serve several local AI models

ease.reason: The described deployment stack needs substantial infrastructure skills.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers may pay for model hosting; no demand is established.

feasibility.reason: The cluster, loaders, API, and monitoring exceed a credible beginner two-week build.

autonomy.reason: Model deployment can repeat automatically, but operations and failures need expertise.

evidence.reason: The maker reports a running cluster and conformance results; independently unverified.

candidates.reason: Infrastructure complexity makes a beginner-sized two-week version unsupported.

candidates.title: BraiNOTES — annotate lecture PDFs in-browser

ease.reason: A browser-only annotation prototype is approachable, though pen input adds work.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: students may pay; this source does not establish demand.

feasibility.reason: A limited PDF annotation prototype appears feasible, but polish across devices is hard.

autonomy.reason: The core is a user-operated editor, with no recurring autonomous business loop shown.

evidence.reason: The maker describes a static browser tool and personal use, not broader adoption.

candidates.reason: A useful editor is plausible, but this is mainly a user-operated tool rather than an autonomous business loop.

candidates.title: VendIQ — automate vendor follow-ups

ease.reason: A narrow follow-up workflow is approachable only with vendor system access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: operations teams may pay; this listing gives no buyer evidence.

feasibility.reason: A mock workflow may fit two weeks; real integrations are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: Reminders can recur, but vendor communication needs human review.

evidence.reason: The supplied text is only a title and product URL, with no working details.

candidates.reason: Insufficient evidence: source snapshot provides only a title and product URL.

candidates.title: Waystone — replay a recorded browser workflow

ease.reason: Recording a simple workflow is plausible, but browser automation has edge cases.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small teams may pay; the source establishes no demand.

feasibility.reason: A narrow demonstration could fit two weeks; the source gives no implementation detail.

autonomy.reason: A recorded task could run repeatedly, but failures and account actions need oversight.

evidence.reason: The source provides only a title and product URL, not operational evidence.

candidates.reason: Insufficient evidence: source snapshot provides only a title and product URL.

candidates.title: Agent PR Gate — limit AI-generated pull requests

ease.reason: A simple repository guard is possible, though GitHub workflow knowledge is needed.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: repository maintainers may pay; no demand is evidenced.

feasibility.reason: A small rule checker may fit two weeks, but product behavior is not described.

autonomy.reason: Automated checks can repeat; maintainers must decide what to merge.

evidence.reason: The snapshot gives only a title and repository link, with no demo details.

candidates.reason: Insufficient evidence about working behavior; source has only a title and repository URL.

candidates.title: Suta — a design skill for generated interfaces

ease.reason: A prompt or design guide is accessible, but usefulness depends on manual prompting.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: builders may pay; the source gives no demand evidence.

feasibility.reason: A small design guide is feasible, though this is not a product workflow description.

autonomy.reason: The skill assists a person rather than showing an autonomous recurring loop.

evidence.reason: The source contains only a title and repository URL, not a demonstrated result.

candidates.reason: Insufficient evidence of a demonstrated product or recurring autonomous loop.

candidates.title: Apify — marketplace for web automation tools

ease.reason: Building a marketplace requires supply, payments, and platform operations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers may pay for automation tools; the source gives platform claims, not student demand.

feasibility.reason: Replicating a broad marketplace is far beyond a two-week beginner scope.

autonomy.reason: The platform describes recurring hosted actors, but platform operations remain substantial.

evidence.reason: The product page describes a working marketplace and reports maker claims; not independently verified here.

candidates.reason: A broad marketplace is not a feasible two-week beginner project.

steps.message: Reviewed eight distinct research candidates against the five-criterion policy. No nonduplicate idea has enough evidence and a sufficiently feasible autonomous loop to support a publishable post at the current threshold; specific evidence and feasibility gaps are recorded above.
